It was an intimate dining experience sitting at the chef’s table, watching each of our dishes be prepared meticulously with the utmost care. We enjoyed the Magical Ticket, and it truly lived up to its name.

The food was delectable, and the menu was incredibly memorable from start to finish. It’s saying something when we tried to rank our favourite courses, and the perfectly cooked A5 Wagyu imported from Japan somehow managed to end up at the bottom!

Each dish was explained to us in depth, and we thoroughly enjoyed the passion and love for the food and culture that Chef Khoa, Chef Trong, and Chef An shared with us. The wait staff were also incredibly attentive and friendly. We truly felt as though we had been welcomed into their home.

The head chef was away during our time here, but he should be so proud of the level of quality and service that his team provided that night. Well done, and we’ll be back next time we’re in town to try the Exhibition menu!

Definitely one the worlds best. Flavours you won’t get elsewhere.
Apr 2025 • Couples
Our friend told us about this restaurant when he visited a few weeks before we arrived and I am so glad we booked.

From the moment I booked via google their communication was amazing. They contacted me directly to pay the deposit and check everything with the booking. We then realised we may be affected by the 50th reunification celebrations and they went above and beyond to offer to hold 2 dates for us in case we couldn’t make the first! In the end we confirmed the initial date worked and had no issues. All the road closures meant we headed to the area earlier to find the place and enjoy some of the events that night. We took up their offer for transport back after the dinner to our hotel which was much easier than waiting for a taxi and a lively way to end the evening.

The entrance is 91 Mac Thi Buoi St - just look for the number on the building. There will be a staff member waiting for you to take you up. Do not look for any sign for the restaurant just the door number. You will be whisked up a couple of flights of stairs to the modern open kitchen restaurant. When booking you can either get a private table or sit at the chefs table (the pass), with the chefs and watch them prepare the food and have greater interaction. We went for the chefs table as we love to watch and interact, and have paid extra for this opportunity several times around the world and in London were we live.

The service is impeccable from entrance to getting home. Attentive but not overbearing. Helpful, especially when choosing wines with the fun of trying to work out price conversions. The descriptions of each course balanced but with the opportunity to ask for greater detail, ingredients and ways they prepared.

Visit the high tech toilet that matches the modern design.

We had the 10 course magical ticket menu which lives up to its magical name. I would highly recommend always booking the higher number of dishes option - if you can - as each dish is a marvel and deserves to be tasted. I am sure whatever menu is on offer will be as amazing.

Each dish was a piece of art. You almost don’t want to eat them. Each mouthful was a journey of flavours perfectly balanced. The portions as you can tell from photos are small but this means you are not having to force yourself at the end which we had had to do in other tasting menus.

Tommy our waiter for the evening really and truly looked after us. Answering our additional questions on the foods and those he could not one of the heads chefs would be over in a flash ready to chat.

The wine list has prices to suit most budgets and a good selection of glasses for those not wanting a full bottle.

I am surprised they don’t have a Michelin star as I am not sure what more they need to do. Up there with the very best fine dining experiences in the world - take our world for it as we eat out in London weekly and travel extensively often just for food.

We do like their early Christmas lunch. Probably best to come during off-peak hours.
Dec 2021
Restaurant setting:

We came for Christmas lunch one week before Christmas, and almost had the entire restaurant to ourselves save for one other table. It wasn't a big restaurant, just a few tables on each floor, but we loved that we were seated near the full glass windows on the third floor as we had a view of Nguyen Hue Walking Street from our seats. And though the restaurant ain't big, they still managed to (1) Squeeze in a two-storey tall Christmas tree in their lobby and (2) Have a full open kitchen bar where customers can see witness the chefs busy plating the dishes. We also liked that they got fresh roses and glass Christmas tree candle holders as part of their table setting! Love their meticulous plating (e.g. chocolate snowman with "coconut scarf") served on their gorgeous plates (e.g. plate that looked like a thick pile of snow)... super cute! Service staff were patient to explain what various ingredients were... and even gave us some extra gooseberries to try!

Food itself:

Well, it is true that their portions are small. I guess that's normal for fine dining? Good to set the right expectations (or have a full breakfast) before you come. While their prices of 390,000VND for the normal set, and 590,000VND for the Christmas set may be a little higher than the Western cafes nearby, but I dare say their food is indeed more creative and prettier than others for this price range. The use of mango slices, gooseberries, soybeans and greek yoghurt (though they ain't expensive ingredients) do help to elevate the dishes when put together well. Their Duck Confit and Iberico Pork were prepared to perfection, in terms of texture and tenderness. The moist pappardelle pasta paired with enoki mushrooms was so tasty that our kids had fun slurping them down. With the inclusion of the mocktails, we honestly thought the price of their delicious lunch sets were very worth it.

Dear Mrs Ly,

We are very sorry that our service did not meet your expectation. We also appreciate your feedback and it definitely helps us to improve our service and guest experience. Moreover, we recognise you as one of our frequent customers and it is our pleasure that you enjoyed our food. At The Monkey Gallery, we strive to balance between three elements: taste, guest experience and our service. We sincerely apologise again that our service did not live up to your standard on this occasion; however, we are still in our soft opening phase and our restaurant is only one month old so we do need time to work on what we are lacking.

Regarding the sharing plate issue, we do not offer sharing plate as our restaurant only serves a course and degustation menu. Each dish comes with specific tablewares from our chef for a unique individual experience. As you mentioned our food portion is small, and just like other fine dining restaurants our course menu is designed for one person and it is not meant to be shared. We are happy if you want to share our dishes but please understand it would undermine your experience and it is not the image we are aiming for at the moment. We also have specific rules from our head chef and owners so our manager and staff could not provide you a sharing plate at the time.

Your bill included a standard 3 course menu for 2 people plus additional A5 Wagyu Beef, Patagonian Toothfish, Lobster Pasta and a bottle of wine which came to a total of 4.9 million VND (approximately US$215). Please understand we only use the most premium ingredients and we try our best to offer the best price to our customers; considering our location is at the corner of Nguyen Hue - Mac Thi Buoi St which is one of the most exclusive street locations in Vietnam.

We do accept your feedback that we are falling short in our services and we hope you will give us another chance to deliver an exceptional service for you and your partner with your next visit to our restaurant. We guarantee that your fourth visit will be an unforgettable one.
